name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd.
business_summary: Murugappa-group electrical-equipment maker (Tube Investments is the majority shareholder; promoter group 56.34%). Two segments: Power Systems (power and distribution transformers, switchgear, ~47% of Q2 FY27 sales, margin 25.9%) and Industrial Systems (LT/HT motors, drives, fans, railway traction and signalling, ~53% of sales). Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): consolidated revenue Rs 3,802 cr (+30%), EBITDA Rs 621 cr (16.3%), PAT Rs 409 cr (+44%), order intake Rs 8,485 cr (+78%), backlog Rs 23,646 cr (+58%). Debt-free; building a semiconductor OSAT business. Largest export order: ~Rs 900 cr of transformers for a US hyperscale data centre.

cost_structure.note: CRGO and structural steel, model estimate

exposures.mechanism: Power Systems (transformers, switchgear) Q2 FY27: sales Rs 1,769 cr (+41%), EBITDA margin 25.9% (21.5% a year ago), order intake +137% to Rs 6,258 cr, backlog Rs 18,964 cr (+81%). Power Systems ~47% of sales and ~75% of EBITDA. Theme +1 SSU (a step-up in transmission/distribution capex intensity) -> +10% power systems volume and +1pp margin -> segment EBITDA +14% = group +10%; x0.97 EV/MCap x persistence 1.0 (structural, visibility 'until FY36' per YES Securities) discounted 50% for capacity/competition = +5.0. High valuation (91x) already prices much of this.

evidence.note: Power systems sales +41%, EBITDA margin 25.9%, order intake +137%, backlog +81% to Rs 18,964 cr
Analysts: multi-year grid modernisation opportunity; YES Securities sees visibility until FY36

exposures.mechanism: PGCIL/state transmission utilities, railways (traction motors), metros and water are ~45% of revenue. +10% government capex growth -> +4% revenue; contribution ~30% vs 16% EBITDA margin -> EBITDA +7.5%; x0.97 x persistence 0.5 = +3.6. Management cites long execution timelines for large railway/transformer contracts, not weak demand.

evidence.note: Double-digit growth in Power Systems and Motion; long execution timelines for railway and transformer contracts

exposures.mechanism: Industrial Systems (LT motors, HT motors, drives, fans; Q2 sales +25% to ~Rs 2,000 cr) ~54% of revenue: market share 38-39% in LT motors, 19-20% in HT motors (YES Securities). +10pp private capex -> +4% revenue; gearing 1.9x -> EBITDA +7.5%; x0.97 x0.5 = +3.5.

evidence.note: CG leads LT motors with 38-39% share and 19-20% in HT motors

exposures.mechanism: Largest-ever order: ~Rs 900 cr of power transformers for a US hyperscale data-centre project; export order inflow ~+84% y/y from a low base (Trade Brains). Theme +1 SSU -> DC share of revenue +4pp at 28% contribution -> EBITDA +7%; x0.97 x0.3 (project-based, lumpy) = +2.0.

evidence.note: ~Rs 900 cr power-transformer order for a US hyperscale data-centre project; export inflows ~+84%

exposures.mechanism: Global AI capex drives US transformer demand and sentiment; SBI Securities notes 'slowdown in AI capex could impact near-term sentiment'. +10% AI capex growth -> +1pp CG revenue... -> +1.5 incl. multiple effect. Overlaps with T_DATA_CENTRES_IN and F_US_EQUITIES; Director should net.

evidence.note: SBI Securities: slowdown in AI capex could impact near-term sentiment

exposures.mechanism: Pack empirical +2.10 per +5% S&P 500 (t +2.2; beta to Nifty 0.95): CG trades as an AI-capex/US-risk-appetite proxy. Shrunk to +1.0 because part of it is the AI-capex edge. S&P is at 7,689 (+1.2% since June).

Copper (winding wire, busbars) ~14% of sales. +10% -> 1.4% of sales -> EBITDA -9% pre; large orders are hedged at booking and have price-variation clauses: ~75% recovered -> -2.3%; x0.97 x0.4 = -0.9, trimmed to -0.5 given the Q2 margin expansion despite copper. Pack empirical is positive (+1.45, t +1.6): copper acts as an electrification-cycle proxy; range crosses zero.

Aluminium (motor frames, castings) ~3% of sales; +10% -> -2% EBITDA pre; 60% recovered; x0.97 x0.4 = -0.3. Pack empirical is strongly POSITIVE (+2.84 per +10%, t +2.6), reflecting the cycle proxy; the cost channel is kept small and negative with a range reaching +1.5. Aluminium is -19.6% since June.

CRGO electrical steel (transformer cores; largely imported) and structural steel ~12% of sales. +10% -> 1.2% of sales -> -7.5% EBITDA pre; ~70% recovered -> -2.3%; x0.97 x0.4 = -0.9. Pack empirical -0.79 per +10% (t -0.7), consistent.

Imports of CRGO/components ~20% of sales vs exports growing (US order Rs 900 cr; ~15% of power systems). Net import ~10% of sales: +3% -> 0.3% of sales -> -1.9% EBITDA pre; half hedged -> -1%; x0.97 x0.4 = -0.4, offset by export upside -> -0.3.
Debt-free; P/E 91x, 14.7x book - long-duration equity. +25bp -> -1.1% value from discount rate plus -0.2 from slower private capex. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 2026-10-07.

Semiconductor (OSAT, Sanand; ISM scheme incentives) and electrical-equipment incentives: 'emerging businesses of semiconductor design and manufacturing are future growth drivers' (SBI Securities). +1 (expansion/disbursement) -> pilot-to-volume transition sooner; est. +1.2% equity value (option value, not near-term EBITDA).

evidence.note: Semiconductor design and manufacturing named a future growth driver

exposures.mechanism: Railways (traction motors, transformers, signalling) ~8% of revenue; +10% rail capex -> +0.8% revenue -> EBITDA +1.5% x0.97 x0.4 = +0.6.

evidence.note: Long execution timelines for large railway contracts

exposures.mechanism: Renewable evacuation and substation build-outs drive transformer/switchgear orders (~15% of Power Systems). +1 SSU stronger support -> +5% power systems volume -> EBITDA +3.5% group x0.97 x0.3 = +1.0.

evidence.note: Analysts cite transmission expansion and renewable integration

exposures.mechanism: Pack empirical -4.42 per +3% USD/CNY (t -1.8). Plausible channel: weaker yuan makes Chinese motors/transformers cheaper in tenders, plus Asia risk-sentiment. Shrunk to about one quarter.
